supporting_observations.claim: Zeek records show WS-LMARTINS-01 making connections to the explicit proxy at 13:36, 13:41, 13:46, 13:51, 13:55, 14:00, and 14:06 UTC. Several are spaced roughly five minutes apart, consistent with the reported periodicity.
The repeated connections include similar byte counts, but the Zeek records identify the proxy endpoint (10.40.20.30:8080), not the external HTTPS destination or the originating process.

known_telemetry_limitations: The collection-status information reports a log collection outage from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC for winsec and Sysmon on WS-LMARTINS-01 and for proxy logs. Consequently, there is no collected process attribution or proxy destination detail for the alerted interval.

Zeek connection and DNS sensors are reported as available, but the supplied connection records show only connections to the internal proxy; they do not identify the tunneled external HTTPS destinations.
claims_not_established: Whether the periodic connections went to the approved PixelForge update service or to another destination.
Which process initiated the periodic connections during the collection outage.
Whether the connections transferred malicious content or involved command-and-control activity.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain proxy logs for 13:30–14:10 UTC, including CONNECT destinations, tunnel identifiers, and request details.
Obtain endpoint process/network telemetry and PixelForge updater logs for the same interval to attribute the connections and verify the destination.
Check the installed PixelForge updater binary and update history on WS-LMARTINS-01 for evidence of an update check or download during the alert window.
unrelated_findings: At 14:13 UTC, outside the alert window, leo.martins used Chrome to access calendar.google.com and related Google static assets. This does not establish that the alerted periodic connections were related to that browsing activity. (T035-00319, T035-00320, T035-00324, T035-00327, T035-00328, T035-00329)
